phase_0.boundary_condition: The ZFC axiomatic framework containing additive combinatorics
phase_0.domain_name: Proof that for any sum-free set S there exists
phase_0.justification: Auto-designed by the native Ob3ect Auto-Designer (in-process candle, no Python)

AFWD.chosen_element: The mapping from S to its complement S-complement
AFWD.justification: A directed transformation moving from the restricted set to the target space

AREV.chosen_element: The inverse projection of sums back into the candidate set
AREV.justification: A descent from the sum-set space back to the individual elements for verification

CLINK.chosen_element: The sequential application of the pigeonhole principle
CLINK.justification: The composition of multiple logical steps to narrow the search space for A

ENGAGR.chosen_element: The boundary elements of S and S-complement
ENGAGR.justification: The simultaneous consideration of elements as both potential members of A and constraints on S

EVALF.chosen_element: The condition where a sum in A plus A falls within S
EVALF.justification: The negative state indicating a failure of the sum-free complement property

EVALT.chosen_element: The condition where A plus A is a subset of S-complement
EVALT.justification: The affirmative success state where the required property is satisfied

FFUSE.chosen_element: The union of the partitioned logic into a single existence proof
FFUSE.justification: The reconstitution of the total space to show the property holds across the entire domain

FSPLIT.chosen_element: The bifurcation of the integer space into S and S-complement
FSPLIT.justification: The division of the domain into two distinct logical paths for analysis

IFIX.chosen_element: The fixed constant c representing the cardinality of A
IFIX.justification: The permanent numerical value that defines the size of the constructed set

IMSCRIB.chosen_element: The identity of the set S as sum-free
IMSCRIB.justification: The self-referential property where S contains no x, y such that x plus y equals z in S

TANCH.justification: The final boundary where the existence of A is verified and the proof closes

VINIT.chosen_element: The empty set and the universe of integers
VINIT.justification: The initial state before the selection of any specific subset or property

phase_2.fuse_element: The logical synthesis of the existence proof
phase_2.fuse_result: The universal set of integers Z
phase_2.split_element: The partition of the universe into S and S-complement
phase_2.split_input: The universal set of integers Z

phase_3.both_description: The superposition of candidate elements before the selection of A is finalized
phase_3.false_description: The non-existence or contradiction of the subset condition
phase_3.true_description: The existence of a set A of size c satisfying the subset condition
phase_3.void_description: The undefined state before the set S is specified

steps.domain_action: Define the universe of integers and the existence of a subset S
Assert the sum-free property of S where no two elements sum to a third
Partition the universe into the set S and its complement S-complement
Identify the density of S-complement within the integer range
Construct a candidate set A by selecting elements from the complement
Apply the Hardy-Littlewood circle method to estimate sum distributions
Branch on the cardinality of the constructed set A
Cardinality of A equals the required constant c
Compute the sum-set A plus A
Verify that every element of A plus A resides in S-complement
Detect any element of A plus A residing in S
Backtrack to re-select elements for A to avoid S
Rejoin the cardinality and subset branches into a single candidate
Hold the density constraints and the sum-free property in simultaneous tension
Fix the specific construction of A as a permanent mathematical object
Reconstitute the partition logic into the final existence theorem
Seal the proof as a completed logical boundary
